text: #730, step 5 of #667's plan and its last, recorded at #735's merge. Refines D-0353, D-0355, D-0362 and D-0368. The dashboard's proposal comparisons and option previews share one cache lifecycle: lookup, atomic saving, installation, restoration and retirement, each kind keeping its own validator and native script-free renderer. Reuse is keyed by the complete detached input record and the current validation and rendering contract, so an identical record is validated, rendered and saved once, concurrent requests included, and any changed input misses even when statement hashes or reader fingerprints match. A failed save keeps the page usable and is retried. Identities still bind evidence and rendered bytes, so unchanged pages keep their bytes, URLs and ETags. Restart checks each saved record against its card, builds it once and installs it without rewriting its file; damaged or obsolete records get isolated diagnostics, and receipt damage still rejects the whole saved snapshot with archive retry. A snapshot is now published only after it and its evidence are on disk: a failed write keeps serving the previous snapshot. Only after a successful publication or restoration are unreachable pages, lookups and evidence files removed, and every page a live card, sibling or receipt references stays, so an immutable URL never changes contents. The first build stopped on two defects in its own acceptance tests, an unused import and a fixture whose comparison could never validate; the plan was revised for only those, and the rebuild passed. The merger ran both browser checks on #735's head with Google Chrome 156 and the dashboard package in 123 s, and, after the merge, the package under the race detector on main: 178 tests passed with no data race in 26 minutes. That run had doubled since #721's 12 minutes, mostly from #728's receipt comparison tests, so the documented race command now allows 40 minutes.
